bug_semantics: CWE-297: default TLS RemoteCertificateValidationCallback in the Couchbase .NET SDK accepted a server certificate whenever the chain could be built against bundled/user CAs, without failing on SslPolicyErrors.RemoteCertificateNameMismatch unless a user-supplied callback was set. After NCBC-3173, ConnectionFactory and CouchbaseHttpClientFactory installed that callback whenever Kv/HttpCertificateCallbackValidation was null: IgnoreNameMismatch only short-circuited the ignore-true path, then ValidateWithDefaultCertificates/GetValidatorWithPredefinedCertificates returned chain.Build(cert) and never consulted the name-mismatch bit. A MITM with any cert chaining to the trusted/Capella CA therefore passed hostname verification. Compounding this, ClusterOptions.ForceIpAsTargetHost defaulted to true (NCBC-2959; IP was hardcoded as AuthenticateAsClient targetHost from SDK3 SSL wiring), so even .NET's built-in name check was bound to the peer IP rather than the configured hostname.
flaw_origin: NCBC-3173 (35aefa5dfddc97f6e289a8a62d97d64fb415c7da) first wrote the default custom validators and wired them as the SslStream/HttpClient callback so Capella's bundled CA would be trusted. The commit intended to 'respect' IgnoreRemoteCertificateNameMismatch, but the non-ignore path delegated to chain-only validation (GetValidatorWithPredefinedCertificates returns built with no hostname test; ValidatorWithIgnoreNameMismatch also cleared RemoteCertificateChainErrors). Immediate parent 867e88ebc789234fa0fc5d32e27ef26c657c2117 still constructed SslStream with the user callback only (null => .NET default hostname verification). Later NCBC-3192 removed the Capella-only InvalidArgumentException so the same callback became the default for all TLS; NCBC-3497/NCBC-3760 refactored logging and custom-cert fallbacks but did not add a name check. NCBC-3993 is the first commit that fails closed on RemoteCertificateNameMismatch when ignore is false.

reasoning: CVE-2025-49015 / GHSA-px2c-r924-mwcc is a real, published CWE-297 in CouchbaseNetClient < 3.7.1: the SDK's default TLS callback did not fail closed on certificate hostname mismatch, so a trusted-chain cert for the wrong host was accepted. The GHSA-cited patch is NCBC-3993 (04d1679 on the 3.7.1 line, cherry-picked from af8e1fa). Working backward from the removed fall-through (`ValidatorWithIgnoreNameMismatch` then `GetValidatorWithDefaultCertificates`/`ValidateWithDefaultCertificates`), git log -S and parent-tree checks show those validators and the default ConnectionFactory/HttpClientFactory wiring were first written in NCBC-3173 35aefa5d; they are absent at parent 867e88eb, which still used a null/.NET-default SslStream callback. 35aefa5d is a single-parent Gerrit change, not a move, revert, or squash aggregate. NCBC-3192 only widened who hit that already-written callback. Tag membership: BIC is in 3.3.0 and 3.7.0 and not in 3.2.9; the 3.7.1 tag contains 04d1679 and 3.7.0 does not. Vendor's 3.0.x–3.2.x listing tracks the related IP-as-TLS-targetHost default (hardcoded in 3.0, ForceIpAsTargetHost=true from 3.2.1), which the CVE text also names; that option was not the code NCBC-3993 changed and stayed true until 3.7.2.
